title: COMMUNICATION FROM THE CHAIR, ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT COMMITTEE, relative to increases in water and electricity rates, utility billing practices, rate…
text:
[Council File 26-1504]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Not Been Held - (10 Votes Required for Consideration)]
COMMUNICATION FROM THE CHAIR, ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT COMMITTEE, relative to increases in water and electricity rates, utility billing practices, rate structures, and programs to assist customers in reducing utility usage.
Recommendation(s) for Council action, pursuant to Motion (Blumenfield, et al. – Jurado):
1. REQUEST the Department of Water and Power (DWP) to report in 30 days with:
a. Factors that have led to increases in water and electricity rates over the past ten years, since the 2016 rate increases, and a comparison of typical bills in the ten hottest neighborhoods in the City.
b. Options for aligning rate structure to encourage optimal power usage, including timing and location of smart meter installation and shift toward time-of-use metering.
c. Reasons why customers whose meters are accessible might receive bills with estimated rather than actual usage, or miss entire billing cycles; how DWP ensures that in such circumstances actual usage is not billed in a higher rate tier; and how DWP might proactively inform customers of payment programs.
d. Feasibility of detecting anomalous water and/or electricity usage before the end of a billing cycle, and proactively informing customers, and/or allowing customers to receive frequent updates regarding actual utility usage.
e. Programs to assist customers in reducing water and electricity usage, including energy audits and energy-efficiency programs; and options for proactively providing information about these programs to lower-income households or communities, or customers with higher usage.
2. REQUEST that LADWP include in this report a transparent breakdown of the effective residential rate per kilowatt-hour ($/kWh) specifically isolating how non-base formulaic pass-through adjustments-such as the Variable Energy Adjustment (VEA), Reliability Cost Adjustment (RCA), and Capped Renewable Energy Adjustment (CREA)-escalated total customer bills independent of base rates and actual household power consumption.
3. REQUEST the Office of the Ratepayer Advocate to review, check, and verify DWP's data, methodology, and findings.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
Neither the City Administrative Officer nor the Chief Legislative Analyst has completed a financial analysis of this report.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
summary: Asks for reports on recent water and electricity rate increases, utility billing practices and rate structures, and on programs to help customers cut their usage.
